scope: Same successful 512-entry local directory model, hidden entries included, all raw names/types/labels and sorted completeness compared. Direct scan versus one supervised same-binary process per query, existing binary pipe/cancel/cleanup adapter, no GUI/SSH or pool integration. Both retain one prewarmed expected listing outside timing. Two process trials per mode warm up; five alternating measured pairs, 50 queries per trial after two unmeasured queries. Generated private files, no payload read. Parent and owned child RSS separately sampled every5ms; sums may double-count shared pages and miss short helper peaks. Per-PID observed CPU maxima are a lower bound over whole trial including harness/setup, NOT full CPU accounting or isolated query CPU. Direct scan lacks process cancellation and is not a fault-equivalent alternative. No native window, whole-process requested-byte proof, stuck kernel filesystem, Windows runtime, long run or default adoption claim.
